title: AI additional reader found 0.7-1.6 extra cancers per 1,000 in prospective Hungarian mammography screening rollout
summary: Ng et al. prospectively assessed a commercial AI system as an additional reader beside standard double reading in three rollout phases (about 25,000 women, four sites), finding 0.7-1.6 additional cancers per 1,000 cases, 0.16-0.30 percent additional recalls and a 0.1-1.9 percent gain in positive predictive value after 7-11 percent additional human reads. Most extra cancers were invasive and small. Authors are from the vendor, Kheiron Medical Technologies; there is no randomization or mortality outcome, and the extra reading workload is part of the result. Abstract-level review.

evidence.tested: Performance was assessed prospectively across a pilot, a multicentre pilot and a live rollout (per abstract).
evidence.unknown: Long-term outcomes, interval cancers and independent evaluation were not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: The AI flagged cases for arbitration review in addition to two human readers.

source_review.scope: abstract and bibliographic metadata (Europe PMC) only; Methods and full text not assessed
